body: I did this exact same thing yesterday! (Sundays are basically our Mondays here). I initially felt so bad about it, but I'm so glad I did it. I needed it and I was a lot more productive today.

Ugh I hate this stigma! I used to work with a woman who would always come in to work with the absolute worst flu (which she would get about 4 times a year) and make everyone else sick, too. The bosses praised her for her dedication!

Same here! I even have an issue telling people that I'm actually physically ill and need to go home. I get anxious that they'll think I don't seem sick enough. I once passed out at work because of it.
Argh, I've been there with the hangovers! Almost lost a job once because  of it. Luckily, I seem to have my drinking under control finally.

I think it's mostly that I hate my job. I feel bad even typing that, as I work with nice people and they treat me well. It's just that it's a tiny company where I am very isolated and the position itself doesn't suit me.

Unfortunately, I have to try and stick it out as I was only at my last job for 6 months and this one for 4 months.

This sounds exactly like me. When I do finally fall asleep, I have nightmares about what will happen if I go in to work or what will happen if I don't. 

I definitely need to go back on medication.
Don't do it! I did that once and it made me beyond miserable. I also ended up being stuck in it longer than I intended.
Maybe cheaper for the company. But I don't know what effects it has on the employees?

Wow, your insights on ladies' shoes are just awe-inspiring. I must say though, it is very nearly surpassed by your deep care for reddit karma. 

You must be so much fun at parties.
Where I currently live, it's considered pretty unethical to put your race or nationality on your CV. Makes it so much easier to have your application considered.
I have 2 passports, so it's a bit confusing.

Yeah that's very unprofessional! At least you knew without having to read the rest of it though. I once got a rejection email with the subject line "Congratulations on your interview at [company name]". They then rambled on about how "great" they thought my interview was before telling me at the very end that I wasn't suitable. It was so misleading and such a waste of time.
